# Command reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.sh from --help output. Do not edit by hand. -->

Three binaries:

| Binary | Runs on | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`zknbe`](#zknbe--device-client) | the machine being protected | bind volumes, unlock, heartbeat agent |
| [`zknbed`](#zknbed--key-server) | the key server | holds per-device keys, enforces policy |
| [`zknbectl`](#zknbectl--key-server-administration) | the key server (or via SSH tunnel) | tokens, devices, audit |

Durations accept `90`, `90s`, `15m`, `4h`, `7d`.

## `zknbe` — device client

### `zknbe`

```text
Network-bound disk encryption with zero-knowledge key servers

Usage: zknbe [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  enroll   Enrol with key servers and write the binding to a state file
  unlock   Obtain the key from the key servers and print it on stdout
  status   Show the binding and the live status on every key server
  rotate   Rotate the per-device key on every reachable key server now
  agent    Run the heartbeat agent (renews leases, rotates keys, reacts to revocation)
  luks     Bind, open and inspect LUKS2 volumes
  tpm      Seal or unseal the device secret with the TPM
  askpass  Answer systemd password prompts for bound volumes (used in the initramfs)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

### `zknbe luks`

```text
Bind, open and inspect LUKS2 volumes

Usage: zknbe luks [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  bind        Enrol with key servers and add a network-bound keyslot to a LUKS2 volume
  open        Unlock a bound volume and map it as /dev/mapper/NAME
  passphrase  Print the passphrase of a bound volume (for crypttab keyscripts)
  unbind      Remove the binding: destroy the keyslot and the token
  status      Show the binding stored in a volume header
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### `zknbe luks bind`

```text
Enrol with key servers and add a network-bound keyslot to a LUKS2 volume

Usage: zknbe luks bind [OPTIONS] --server <SERVERS> <DEVICE>

Arguments:
  <DEVICE>

Options:
      --name <NAME>            Device name shown to administrators (defaults to the host name)
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
  -t, --threshold <THRESHOLD>  Number of key servers that must cooperate to unlock (default: all of them)
  -s, --server <SERVERS>       A key server and its single-use enrolment token, as URL=TOKEN. Repeat per server
      --keyslot <KEYSLOT>      Keyslot to use (default: first free)
      --key-file <KEY_FILE>    Existing key file authorising the change (default: prompt for a passphrase)
      --tpm2-pcrs <TPM2_PCRS>  Seal the device secret to the TPM, bound to these PCRs (e.g. 7 or 7+11)
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

### `zknbe luks open`

```text
Unlock a bound volume and map it as /dev/mapper/NAME

Usage: zknbe luks open [OPTIONS] <DEVICE> <NAME>

Arguments:
  <DEVICE>
  <NAME>

Options:
      --retry-for <RETRY_FOR>  [default: 0]
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

Options:

### `zknbe enroll`

```text
Enrol with key servers and write the binding to a state file

Usage: zknbe enroll [OPTIONS] --state <STATE> --server <SERVERS>

Options:
      --state <STATE>          Where to write the binding state (must not exist)
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --name <NAME>            Device name shown to administrators (defaults to the host name)
  -t, --threshold <THRESHOLD>  Number of key servers that must cooperate to unlock (default: all of them)
  -s, --server <SERVERS>       A key server and its single-use enrolment token, as URL=TOKEN. Repeat per server
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

### `zknbe unlock`

```text
Obtain the key from the key servers and print it on stdout

Usage: zknbe unlock [OPTIONS] <--state <STATE>|--luks <LUKS>>

Options:
      --state <STATE>          Binding stored in a state file
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --luks <LUKS>            Binding stored in the header of this LUKS2 volume
      --retry-for <RETRY_FOR>  Keep retrying for this long if servers are unreachable (e.g. 2m) [default: 0]
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

### `zknbe status`

```text
Show the binding and the live status on every key server

Usage: zknbe status [OPTIONS] <--state <STATE>|--luks <LUKS>>

Options:
      --state <STATE>      Binding stored in a state file
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --luks <LUKS>        Binding stored in the header of this LUKS2 volume
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### `zknbe rotate`

```text
Rotate the per-device key on every reachable key server now

Usage: zknbe rotate [OPTIONS] <--state <STATE>|--luks <LUKS>>

Options:
      --state <STATE>      Binding stored in a state file
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --luks <LUKS>        Binding stored in the header of this LUKS2 volume
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### `zknbe agent`

```text
Run the heartbeat agent (renews leases, rotates keys, reacts to revocation)

Usage: zknbe agent [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --luks <LUKS>              LUKS2 volume to look after (repeatable). Default: all bound volumes found
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>        Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --state <STATE>            State file to look after (repeatable)
      --on-revoked <ON_REVOKED>  Shell command to run once this device is revoked beyond recovery, e.g. "systemctl poweroff" [env: ZKNBE_ON_REVOKED=]
      --once                     Run a single cycle and exit (0 healthy, 3 revoked, 4 degraded)
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

### `zknbe tpm seal`

```text
Seal the device secret to this machine's TPM 2.0 (via systemd-creds)

Usage: zknbe tpm seal [OPTIONS] <--state <STATE>|--luks <LUKS>>

Options:
      --state <STATE>      Binding stored in a state file
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --luks <LUKS>        Binding stored in the header of this LUKS2 volume
      --pcrs <PCRS>        PCRs to bind to. 7 = Secure Boot state [default: 7]
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### `zknbe tpm unseal`

```text
Store the device secret unsealed again (e.g. before a firmware update changes PCRs)

Usage: zknbe tpm unseal [OPTIONS] <--state <STATE>|--luks <LUKS>>

Options:
      --state <STATE>      Binding stored in a state file
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>  Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --luks <LUKS>        Binding stored in the header of this LUKS2 volume
  -h, --help               Print help
```

### `zknbe askpass`

```text
Answer systemd password prompts for bound volumes (used in the initramfs)

Usage: zknbe askpass [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --timeout <TIMEOUT>      Per-request network timeout [default: 5s]
      --watch                  Keep running and answer prompts as they appear
      --retry-for <RETRY_FOR>  Without --watch: how long to keep retrying unanswered prompts [default: 2m]
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

## `zknbed` — key server

### `zknbed`

```text
ZK-NBE key server

Usage: zknbed [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>      Path to the configuration file. Built-in defaults are used if it does not exist and the flag was not given explicitly [env: ZKNBED_CONFIG=]
      --data-dir <DATA_DIR>  Override `server.data_dir` [env: ZKNBED_DATA_DIR=]
      --check                Validate the configuration and exit
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

## `zknbectl` — key server administration

### `zknbectl`

```text
Administer a ZK-NBE key server

Usage: zknbectl [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status  Show server identity and device counts
  token   Manage single-use enrolment tokens
  device  Inspect and control enrolled devices
  audit   Read and verify the tamper-evident audit log
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --url <URL>                Admin API base URL [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:7422]
      --token <TOKEN>            Admin token (prefer --token-file or the environment over the command line) [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN]
      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>  File containing the admin token [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE=] [default: /var/lib/zknbe/admin.token]
      --json                     Print raw JSON instead of tables
  -h, --help                     Print help
  -V, --version                  Print version
```

### `zknbectl status`

```text
Show server identity and device counts

Usage: zknbectl status [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --url <URL>                Admin API base URL [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:7422]
      --token <TOKEN>            Admin token (prefer --token-file or the environment over the command line) [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN]
      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>  File containing the admin token [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE=] [default: /var/lib/zknbe/admin.token]
      --json                     Print raw JSON instead of tables
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

### `zknbectl token create`

```text
Create an enrolment token for one device

Usage: zknbectl token create [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>

Options:
      --name <NAME>
          Label for the token (typically the host name)
      --url <URL>
          Admin API base URL [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:7422]
      --token <TOKEN>
          Admin token (prefer --token-file or the environment over the command line) [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN]
      --ttl <TTL>
          Token validity (e.g. 1h) [default: 1h]
      --lease-ttl <LEASE_TTL>
          How long a device may be silent before it is locked (e.g. 15m)
      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>
          File containing the admin token [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE=] [default: /var/lib/zknbe/admin.token]
      --heartbeat <HEARTBEAT>
          Heartbeat interval advertised to the device (e.g. 2m)
      --json
          Print raw JSON instead of tables
      --on-lease-expiry <ON_LEASE_EXPIRY>
          What happens when the lease lapses: lock (default) or allow
      --rotation-interval <ROTATION_INTERVAL>
          Key rotation interval (e.g. 7d); 0 disables rotation
      --allow-cidr <ALLOW_CIDR>
          Restrict requests to this network (repeatable). Replaces the existing list
      --allow-any-network
          Remove any network restriction
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### `zknbectl device approve`

```text
Unlock a locked device, or pre-authorise downtime for an active one

Usage: zknbectl device approve [OPTIONS] <DEVICE>

Arguments:
  <DEVICE>

Options:
      --url <URL>                Admin API base URL [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_URL=] [default: http://127.0.0.1:7422]
      --window <WINDOW>          How long the lease check is waived (e.g. 30m, 4h)
      --token <TOKEN>            Admin token (prefer --token-file or the environment over the command line) [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN]
      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>  File containing the admin token [env: ZKNBE_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE=] [default: /var/lib/zknbe/admin.token]
      --json                     Print raw JSON instead of tables
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

```text

      --json                     Print raw JSON instead of tables

```
